partner_result.premise: For an invertible signature-(2,1) original-coordinate physical triple with majority eigenvalue magnitudes lambda1,lambda2 and minority magnitude mu, the majority output submeasure is dominated by C_+ dx with C_+ <= 2pi/sqrt(lambda1 lambda2), independent of mu; sign-reflected statement likewise.

new_claims.name: minority-null semidefinite endpoint
new_claims.scope: A=[[B,C],[C^T,D]] in original coordinates; B is 3x3 PSD or NSD rank two with nonzero eigenvalue magnitudes lambda1,lambda2; Range(C) subset Range(B); independent cap-one coordinates.

new_claims.name: block-diagonal continuity compiler
new_claims.scope: Above B with C=0 and an independent nonzero quadratic remainder D!=0.
new_claims.conclusion: p_(X^TAX) belongs to C0 and has the same height bound 2pi/sqrt(lambda1 lambda2).

new_claims.name: bounded receiver need not be continuous
new_claims.conclusion: Density of X1^2+X2^2 equals pi on (0,1/4) and zero on (-infinity,0), so no continuous representative.

proof_mechanism: Perturb only the null eigenvalue in the minority sign, apply the partner ruled-majority measure bound uniformly, use range alignment so the completed-square center is epsilon-independent, observe the majority event tends almost surely to the whole space off an affine line of zero product mass, and pass measure domination by weak convergence/Portmanteau.
unresolved_implication: Treat rank-two semidefinite physical blocks whose null direction has non-range-aligned outside coupling n^T C !=0, or route that failure to another original-product smoothing receiver before any worst-fiber conditional supremum; then aggregate across physical triples to reach the bare three-large-eigenvalue hypothesis.
